clue.text: This ban affected the production of alcoholic liquor

indicators.note: affected here means altered or worked upon, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prohibition that changed how a particular spirit was made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' rearranges THIS BAN into the spirit; 'the production of' only joins the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinth is a strong, green, aniseed-flavoured spirit, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: A couple of beasts in need of sorting out!

parts.note: the first beast is a nag, an old horse
the second beast is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: Two animals have got into a mess and need sorting out.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies both NAG and RAM; the definition describes a jumbled word as something needing to be put in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or phrase made by jumbling letters is a puzzle that needs its letters rearranged to be solved.

clue.text: Kind of scouts around the City

indicators.note: around means the word for scouts surrounds the City's letters

parts.note: spies scout out information
EC is the postal district of the City of London

explanation.surface: A type of Scout troop based near central London.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, postcode EC; SPIES goes 'around' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a kind or sort of thing.

clue.text: The drink of an emperor at one time

definitions.meaning: a hot drink of port or sherry with sugar and spices
the title formerly used by the rulers of Ethiopia

explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a spiced hot wine and the old imperial title of Ethiopian kings.

clue.text: A person with a simple remedy for every ill

definitions.text: A person with a simple remedy for every ill

parts.words: A person with a simple remedy for every ill
parts.note: 'simple' is an old noun for a medicinal plant, so this is someone treating illness with plants

explanation.surface: Someone with an easy fix for any ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'simple' was a medicinal plant or a medicine made from one.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person grows or prescribes plants for healing.

clue.text: There are many into delightful needlework

indicators.note: into tells us one piece is placed inside the other, the 'many' going within the word for delightful

parts.note: taking means charming or delightful, as in 'a taking smile'
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: A remark that lots of people are keen on lovely embroidery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There are' is padding; 'into' puts C (Roman 100, 'many') inside TAKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacking is the loose temporary stitching used in sewing to hold fabric before final seams.

clue.text: Backing up expertise of French dealing

indicators.note: in a down clue backing up means the word is read from bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: art means skill or expertise
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A French expert's skill is being supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing up' reverses ART to TRA, then DE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade is buying and selling, dealing in goods.

clue.text: Mason who is by no means an honest guy?

definitions.text: Mason who is by no means an honest guy?

parts.words: Mason who is by no means an honest guy?
parts.note: a stonemason uses a cutting tool on stone, and the same word is slang for a swindler

explanation.surface: A stoneworker turns out to be dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: Mason suggests a Freemason; the reading is a stone carver who uses a chisel, and also a cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheat or swindler, from 'chisel' meaning to defraud, and literally one who carves with a chisel.

clue.text: Hero-worship can make one so idle!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: can make says the following letters can be made into something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: Admiring someone too much can leave a person lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make' rearranges I (one) plus SO IDLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise someone is to worship them as a hero.

clue.text: The old king regards a collar less shirt as most dismal

parts.note: GR, George Rex, stands for an old king
eyes means looks at or regards
a T-shirt has no collar, giving T

explanation.surface: A former monarch looks at a collarless shirt and finds it dreary.
explanation.walkthrough: GR is the cipher of King George; a T-shirt is the shirt without a collar.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey describes dull, cheerless weather or moods; the superlative is most dismal.

clue.text: The man who's returned hurt

parts.note: read 'returned hurt' as paying back an injury in kind rather than coming home wounded

explanation.surface: A man has come back injured.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone back from somewhere with an injury; the cryptic sense is someone who repays a hurt with one of his own.
explanation.definitionFit: One who takes revenge returns an injury on the person who caused it.

clue.text: Fatty is a dope user

indicators.note: the dope is put to use and reworked, signalling that the letters of 'is a dope' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone overweight is accused of taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fatty' looks like an insulting nickname but is the adjective being defined; 'user' makes the letters of IS A DOPE form a new word.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose describes tissue made of or storing body fat.

clue.text: Bring back control-the country's behind it

indicators.note: behind places the word for country after the word for control

parts.note: to rein in is to control, and a rein is a means of control
a state is a country or nation

explanation.surface: An instruction to restore control because the nation supports it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers back to REIN, and STATE sits behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone to a former post is to bring them back.

clue.text: A little spaniel, it emerges, is quite the best

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small dog turns out to be a champion.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'is', but the answer is a noun or adjective, so 'is' links wordplay to 'quite the best'. The run sits in spaniEL, IT Emerges.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the pick of a group, its top members.

clue.text: Love food!

parts.note: recalls Shakespeare's line in Twelfth Night that a certain art is the food of love

explanation.surface: An exclamation of enthusiasm for eating.
explanation.walkthrough: Twelfth Night opens: 'If music be the food of love, play on', so this is food for love.
explanation.definitionFit: Orsino's speech calls melody and song the nourishment that feeds romantic passion.

clue.text: Green gets absorbed in study with little hesitation. He's changed

indicators.note: gets absorbed in means one piece goes inside the others

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
er is the short sound of hesitation
vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: A naive person studies and pauses briefly, then changes.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT, the heraldic word for green, 'gets absorbed in' CON plus ER.
explanation.definitionFit: One who has changed belief is a convert; the clue treats him as one who has turned.

clue.text: Set in order etc. — in order, mind

parts.note: taken as written
to tell someone to do something is to order them

indicators.note: here 'in order' means tidied up, so the letters of etc are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to arrange items and so on properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' places IN first, then TELL ('order'); 'in order' rearranges ETC to ECT.
explanation.definitionFit: The intellect is the faculty of reasoning and understanding, the thinking mind.

clue.text: Sets tales circulating, being quite undiscriminating

indicators.note: circulating means moving around, so the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Spreading gossip shows a lack of judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating' rearranges SETS TALES; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking taste means having no discernment or refinement.

clue.text: Gives about a thousand single commands

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for gives goes round the other letters

parts.note: donates means gives
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
I, the Roman numeral one, stands for single

explanation.surface: Someone hands out about a thousand individual orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps DONATES around M and I.
explanation.definitionFit: To command something is to control or rule over it.

clue.text: Left behind last month-intend to speak out

indicators.note: behind puts the letter for left after the month

parts.note: Dec, December, is the last month of the year
to aim is to intend

explanation.surface: Someone left behind at the end of the year intends to speak up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' places L after DEC; AIM follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim is to speak out rhetorically and loudly.

clue.text: Allude to people turning it on

parts.note: men means people

indicators.note: turning signals the letters of it on are mixed up

explanation.surface: Hinting at people who are switching something on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges IT ON to TION.
explanation.definitionFit: To mention something is to refer briefly to it.

clue.text: Painter holding a carrier for a woman

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the painter's letters wrap around the carrier

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword stand-in for a painter
a hod is a trough on a pole used to carry bricks

explanation.surface: An artist holding a bag or case for a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: A hod is a builder's brick carrier; 'holding' puts it inside RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Cereal given to a lame eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Porridge given to a disabled oddball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges TO A LAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal is ground oats, a cereal food.

clue.text: Checks the result of police work

explanation.definitionFit: To halt something is to stop it, and police detentions of suspects carry the same word.

clue.text: None will go in bamboo boat

indicators.note: will go in signals that one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: bamboo is a kind of cane
O, the figure zero, means none

explanation.surface: A remark that nothing can be fitted into a bamboo vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'None' is O (zero), which goes inside CANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light narrow boat paddled by hand.

clue.text: Tots caper about and she looks on

indicators.note: about here means moving around, shuffling the letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Small children frolic while a woman watches them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges TOTS CAPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is an onlooker who watches an event.

clue.text: One fibre used by weavers is a linen substitute

indicators.note: used by says the answer is contained within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A plant fibre weavers employ as a replacement for linen.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is weaverS IS A Linen.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisal is a strong plant fibre used for rope and matting.

clue.text: Thin, and so light

definitions.meaning: a slender candle or wax-coated wick

explanation.walkthrough: 'and so' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both narrowing gradually and a slender candle used for lighting.

clue.text: Flies through in a back-seat

indicators.note: in places the word for through inside the other letters
back means the word set is read backwards

parts.note: the setter treats seat as the word set; the letters needed are S, E, T
via means through or by way of

explanation.surface: Someone flies while seated in the back of a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SET into TES; A plus TES with VIA put 'in' gives the answer. The printed 'seat' has a stray A: reversed it gives TAES, which cannot fit.
explanation.definitionFit: To aviate is to pilot or travel in an aircraft.

clue.text: Former journalists, say

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
the press is a collective term for journalists

explanation.surface: A reference to journalists who used to work somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is the definition, not an example signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a thought is to put it into words.

clue.text: Ore obtained by a worker underground, a trainee

parts.note: a miner works below ground
L is for learner, as on the L-plate of a learner driver

explanation.surface: Rock is extracted by a pit worker who is still in training.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the learner sign shown on a British learner driver's car.
explanation.definitionFit: Ore is a naturally occurring mineral substance mined for its metal.

clue.text: Walks on the street, then turns

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
rolls means turns over and over

explanation.surface: Someone walks along the road and then spins round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'then' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Strolls are leisurely walks.
